data.text: Extended reality has commercial potential in various sectors, and penetration in the commercial space can be expected both percentage-wise and value-wise. Gaming, healthcare, and education are prominent or emerging domains that use immersive technologies to improve popularity, training, and engagement, although excessive duration may create problems. The automobile, travel, tourism, and digital heritage sectors are evolving or emerging areas that use immersive experiences for virtual exploration. Finally, real estate and architecture allow for the exploration of properties, while defense provides simulations for specialized military training.
points: Extended reality has commercial potential in various sectors, and penetration in the commercial space can be expected both percentage-wise and value-wise.
Gaming and entertainment is a current VR domain that uses immersive technologies to make gaming more acceptable and popular.
Healthcare is a prominent domain for training, and education is an emerging domain that can improve engagement and outcomes, although excessive duration may create problems.
The automobile, travel, tourism, and digital heritage sectors are evolving or emerging areas that use immersive technologies for virtual exploration.
Real estate and architecture allow for exploring properties, while defense is a major area for simulations used in specialized military training.

data.text: Immersion in virtual reality means that the user's senses are blocked from the real-world environment so they receive input only from the virtual world. Systems are categorized into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive based on the degree of sensory blocking. Non-immersive and semi-immersive systems are common and cost-effective, while fully immersive systems are the costliest and rarest because they completely block all senses.
points: Immersion in VR means the user's senses are blocked from the real world so they only receive input from the virtual world.
VR systems are categorized into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems based on the degree of sensory blocking.
Non-immersive systems allow users to control virtual activities while remaining physically attached to the real world.
Semi-immersive systems provide partial immersion by blocking some senses while leaving the user free to sense the real world.
Fully immersive systems completely block all senses but are the costliest and rarest systems.
